channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Ramat Hasharon Torah group sounds the shofar for residents across the city
item.description: Members of Ramat Hasharon’s garin torani sounded the shofar at various locations across the city, reaching residents with the mitzvah of hearing the shofar, including several deeply moving encounters.

item.title: Iran: Israel is the ‘only winner’ of regional tensions
item.description: Tehran calls for dialogue with Gulf states as Saudi Arabia postpones planned Oman meeting, Iran International report says.

item.title: Newsmax: The fight over Israel is entering a new phase
item.description: What happens after the House votes to punish universities that boycott Israel? Newsmax examines the new bill, campus antisemitism, BDS activism, Hamas and Israel’s next moves.

item.title: IAEA: Almost no nuclear inspections in Iran for six months
item.description: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi warns inspectors have had virtually no access to Iran’s nuclear facilities for six months, raising 'serious proliferation' concerns.

item.title: Daycare horror: Assistant jailed for seven years for abusing 12 children
item.description: Daycare assistant Shelly Sheinker sentenced after security cameras capture dozens of incidents of abuse; prosecutors weigh appeal for harsher sentence.

item.title: Paralympic athlete suffers seizure during live TV interview
item.description: Puerto Rican Paralympic athlete Melanie Valdés Reyes suffered an epileptic seizure during a live morning TV interview, then shared the footage to raise awareness about the condition.

item.title: Lahav 433 officer wounded after gun accidentally fires
item.description: Senior police officer lightly injured by discharge from his personal handgun; incident under investigation.

item.title: Modzitz Rebbe hospitalized on Rosh Hashanah, returns to lead prayers
item.description: Modzitz Rebbe is rushed to hospital on Rosh Hashanah, but returns to lead holiday prayers.

item.title: ‘We want justice’: Family of murdered 7-year-old confronts accused killer in court
item.description: Hillel Mordechai Dadon’s family arrived at court as prosecutors filed charges against the man accused of murdering the seven-year-old in Beit Shemesh and attempting to kill his cousin.

item.title: Deadly poolside stabbing: Beit Shemesh man indicted for child’s murder
item.description: Prosecutors reveal chilling details of the attack that killed Hillel Mordechai Dadon and left his cousin hospitalized.

item.title: 23 years after losing his sight in terror attack, Oren gets married
item.description: Twenty-three years after losing his sight and five family members in Maxim's restaurant terror attack, Oren Almog married Rotem Alima in an emotional ceremony featuring a powerful prayer for the restoration of his vision.

item.title: Shot down over Iran: Inside the daring US rescue of ‘Bravo’
item.description: Badly wounded and alone for two days deep inside Iran, the US airman’s rescue triggered a massive operation - and newly-released footage reveals how it unfolded.

item.title: September 10, 2001: the day we lost
item.description: “The day everything changed" became “the day everything went back to how it was before," only even crazier and more suicidal. That morning the Islamist terrorists planted a poisonous seed that continues to grow throughout the West. Opinion.

item.title: 'We got there just in time': Rescuer tells the story of the operation in Colombia
item.description: 'Chances of finding survivors alive were slim. But we knew we would do everything we could to help,' Staff Sgt. (res.) Asaf talks about the complex rescue operation carried out by the Israeli delegation in Colombia.

item.title: IDF thwarts imminent shooting attack in Hebron
item.description: Terrorist arrested on Shabbat after Shin Bet intelligence indicated he was preparing to open fire on Israeli civilians in the immediate future.

item.title: Rome and the West: A slow demise and a horrific suicide
item.description: What ideas define the intellectual and spiritual state of the West today? Only one: Marxist mutations in their most repulsive and absurd forms. And the West opened its doors to fundamentalist Islam, represented by the Muslim Brotherhood and its patrons, most notably Qatar and Turkey. Opinion.

item.title: Two screens, one choice: The lie of ‘Naza’ vs. the truth of ‘Fauda’
item.description: While a libelous Israeli film was rewarded in Venice with a jury prize and a standing ovation, the popular TV series confronts viewers with the truth about Oct. 7. Opinion.

item.title: Study: Yale professor finds ‘deep and systematic’ anti-Israel bias in NYT Gaza coverage
item.description: Study analyzed more than 1,500 articles published between Hamas’ October 7 attack and June 2024, finding Israeli casualties and Palestinian violence were largely overlooked.

item.title: Jewish abortion rights battle reaches Indiana Supreme Court
item.description: A case pitting Indiana Jews against an abortion ban heads back to court.

item.title: Report: Iran turns to Russia for upgraded drones against Israel, US
item.description: Tehran seeking advanced Russian-made versions of its own Shahed drones, report says.

item.title: Clinton reveals: CIA abandoned pre-9/11 plan to take out bin Laden over civilian fears
item.description: Former President Bill Clinton says the CIA scrapped a pre-9/11 operation against Osama bin Laden over fears it could kill innocent civilians.

item.title: Report: Trump administration wants Iran talks focused on nuclear program, not Hormuz
item.description: The Trump administration wants future Iran talks limited to the nuclear issue as Tehran seeks resolution of the Strait of Hormuz dispute, CNN reports.

item.title: Trump praises Kushner, Witkoff on Gaza: Nobody could've done the job
item.description: Trump praises Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff for their Gaza diplomacy, saying they helped secure the hostages' return and advance a ceasefire.

item.title: Fast of Gedaliah times
item.description:
These are the start and end times for the Fast of Gedaliah, being observed on Monday:
Jerusalem: Fast begins - 5:10 a.m. Fast ends - 7:10 p.m.
Tel Aviv: Fast begins - 5:12 a.m. Fast ends - 7:08 p.m.
Haifa: Fast begins - 5:10 a.m. Fast ends - 7:10 p.m.
Tzfat: Fast begins - 5:08 a.m. Fast ends - 7:10 p.m.
Be'er Sheva: Fast begins - 5:12 a.m. Fast ends - 7:10 p.m.
Eilat: Fast begins - 5:12 a.m. Fast ends - 7:06 p.m.

item.title: 'Fauda' Season 5 shocks viewers worldwide with harrowing portrayal of October 7
item.description: "Fauda" Season 5 draws emotional reactions worldwide as episodes depicting October 7 leave viewers shaken and deepen understanding of the massacre.

item.title: Gantz slams anti-Israel film: Liars
item.description: Blue and White chairman Benny Gantz sharply criticizes the film “NAZA", declaring: “Revenge was never the purpose of the fighting."

item.title: New Gaza flotilla raises security concerns
item.description: Israel is holding discussions ahead of a new flotilla expected to depart Italy in late October, while the IDF has already begun initial preparations to stop it.

item.title: IDF responds to Israeli film: "Internal and absurd contradictions"
item.description: IDF responds to claims of war crimes and genocide as presented on Israeli film. "The IDF categorically rejects these allegations"

item.title: CENTCOM commander: 'We're well armed and ready'
item.description: Asked on 60 Minutes about munitions shortages, US Central Command Chief Brad Cooper answered: ""I am not concerned at all. We're well armed and ready for any contingency."

item.title: A good judgment
item.description: G-d is not here to catch us but to help us reach our tikkun, rectification. Each failure is merely a test that we were unable to overcome, but G-d is not done. Another similar test will come our way to see if we can overcome it.
